Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.3% today to close at $388.90, continuing a sharp 7.8% climb over the past two weeks. The gains follow a jump in global diesel prices to record highs, driven by geopolitical disruptions to refinery capacity in Ukraine and Russia — exactly the kind of tight supply environment that benefits a major U.S. refiner. U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity right now, leaving little room to ramp up production, which means higher margins on every barrel processed as demand stays strong and supply from competitors dries up.

The broader backdrop amplifies this advantage: sanctions on Iran are expanding with EU backing, and supply chains for crude are being reshuffled following a U.S. deal with Venezuela, while diesel storage remains lean at 104 million barrels. These geopolitical headwinds are lifting refining margins globally, and MPC's domestic footprint shields it from some of the chaos hitting European and Asian refiners.
